concepts.title: Running a Statistical Project: The Full Pipeline
concepts.definition: This chapter assembles the whole course into a student project: choose a topic, set objectives, design the questionnaire, collect data, organise and present it, apply statistical tools -- percentages, averages, index numbers, correlation -- and end with conclusions and bibliography.
concepts.key_idea: The project is the course in miniature -- one question carried through every statistical stage to a conclusion.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest108.txt project sections (steps of a project, choosing a topic or objective, designing questionnaire, conclusion and bibliography)
question_patterns: list the steps involved in conducting a statistical project
in class 11 use of statistical tools: how should the objective of a study be framed
what makes a good questionnaire for a project
why must a project end with conclusions and bibliography
choose a topic for a survey in your school and outline its design
how does the project integrate all the tools learnt this year

solution_steps.explain: Pick a specific, answerable objective -- vague topics produce unusable data.
Draft the questionnaire with clear, non-leading items and test it before field work.
Analyse the collected data with the course's tools and finish with conclusions tied to the objective and a cited bibliography.

concepts.title: Applying the Tools: Percentages, Averages and Correlation
concepts.definition: On the collected data the student applies the year's toolkit: percentages for composition, mean, median and mode for central tendency, index numbers for change over time and correlation for relationships -- choosing the tool that fits the question rather than using all of them blindly.
concepts.key_idea: Right tool for the right question -- composition asks percentages, centrality asks averages, relationships ask correlation.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest108.txt application sections (percentage calculations, averages, index numbers, correlation in project analysis, interpretation of results)
question_patterns: which statistical tools suit a study of family expenditure and why
in class 11 use of statistical tools: how would you analyse change in prices in your project
use percentages to present the composition of a given budget
apply averages to summarise the collected data
how can correlation be used in a student project
interpret the results of the tools applied in a given study

solution_steps.explain: Composition questions need percentages; typical-value questions need averages; change needs index numbers; association needs correlation.
Apply each tool to the correctly organised data, checking units and bases.
State what the figures show and what they cannot -- limits belong in honest conclusions.

concepts.title: Organising, Presenting and Interpreting Project Data
concepts.definition: Once collected, project data must be classified into a frequency distribution, presented in tables and diagrams, and then interpreted: what the figures mean for the objective, what patterns emerged, and what limitations qualify the conclusions.
concepts.key_idea: Collect is only halfway -- classify, display and interpret turn data into a project's findings.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest108.txt organisation sections (classification of collected data, tabular and diagrammatic presentation, interpretation of results, limitations of the study)
question_patterns: how should collected project data be organised before analysis
in class 11 use of statistical tools: present the given project data as a table and diagram
why must conclusions follow from the objective of the study
what limitations should a project report acknowledge

arrange the analysis stage of a project in correct order

solution_steps.explain: Sort responses into classes and enter totals in a titled table for compact comparison.
Choose a bar diagram, pie chart or polygon that makes the main pattern visible at a glance.
Relate the findings back to the objective, noting sample size and other limitations honestly.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Design a mini-project on the spending habits of classmates: state the objective, the tool of collection and the presentation method.

solution_template.explain: Objective: to study how much students of class 11 spend weekly and on what items.
A short questionnaire administered personally to a sample of 50 students collects the data.
Classified tables, a pie chart of spending shares, and averages conclude the analysis.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Your project data show monthly ice-cream sales and daily temperature for a year. Which tool fits and what would you expect to find?

solution_template.explain: Two quantitative variables varying together call for correlation analysis.
Hotter days selling more ice-cream suggests a positive correlation.
Report the association as correlation -- temperature alone may not be the full cause.
